summary: Session 2 of 3 landed the report-baseline standalone CLI subcommand end-to-end. Composes the S1 ReportBaselineService with three new seams (IReportSource, IReportPdfRenderer, ReportBaselineRunner) plus Windows-only live-COM implementations (AccessReportSpecReader opens reports in hidden design view to read RecordSource + group-level keys via the live Reports collection; AccessReportPdfRenderer wraps DoCmd.OutputTo acOutputReport, name, 'PDF Format (*.pdf)', path). CLI surface matches the spec verbatim: report-baseline --db --out [--reports name,name] [--params <params.json>] [--no-clean] [--json-status]. Exit codes mirror run (0/1/2/3). Per-report artifacts at <out>/AccessMetaData/<dbName>/reports-baseline/<report>/{output.pdf,aggregates.json} plus top-level baseline-manifest.json (deterministic, ordinal-sorted, no wall-clock fields). 18 new tests over the S1 baseline (15 originally planned + 3 R1-remediation), bringing AccessHarvester.Tests to 517 passing / 2 skipped (COM-required) / 0 failed. Cross-provider session-verification took two rounds: R1 ISSUES_FOUND with two Major items (Dictionary-enumeration-order positional binding contract; no stale-output cleanup on rerun) + a both-fail coverage gap + minor doc nits, all addressed in-session; R2 VERIFIED with empty issues. Also landed the deferred-from-S1-R4 ParametersUsed mutation regression test, drift-gate fix to CliUsageTextTests for the new report-baseline heading, and convention-prescribed [Collection('HomeHealthCareCom')] applied to five pre-existing parallel-COM-CLI Integration test classes (knocked Integration project failures 3->1; the remaining SanitizeCommandTests.HomeHealthCare timeout is pre-existing latent slowness in the sanitize CLI path, confirmed via isolation, not introduced by S2). S2 routed cost ~$0.45 (R1+R2 session-verification only; orchestrator-direct for all mechanical implementation work per Delegation Discipline). Integration test scoped via --reports to four srpt* sub-reports because HomeHealthCare's rpt* top-level reports pop modal parameter prompts via DoCmd.OutputTo (parameter elicitation deferred to S3 per Resolved Decision #3). Closes spec.md Session 2 deliverables; ready for S3 (docs, parameter elicitation, golden capture, closeout).

reason.specifics: Session 3 wraps the set: documentation drafting (CLI reference in install.md, interpretation-guide notes on the new subcommand, parameter selection strategy and --params shape), parameter elicitation design + implementation (Forms!/Reports!/TempVars binding shimming OR in-memory RecordSource literal substitution closed with acSaveNo, per the maintainer-validated COM patterns; routes through the existing identify-usage mechanism per Resolved Decision #3), golden capture for NorthwindDevEdition (rptInvoice, rptSalesByEmployee, rptSalesByProduct) plus HomeHealthCare's in-scope reports (srpt* immediately; rpt* after parameter elicitation lands), and the closeout pieces (ROADMAP flip, change-log, disposition.json status=complete, Step 9 reorganization review). The recommended orchestrator is gemini-pro at effort=medium per the original ai-assignment.md plan: docs drafting + mechanical golden capture is the cost-effective profile. The orchestrator should route docs drafting through route(task_type='summarization') (NOT 'documentation', per the convention) and handle file mechanics directly. Open maintainer call to surface during S3 planning: whether to revisit the spec so PDF capture becomes opt-in (--include-pdf) with aggregates-only as the default, given the modal-prompt exposure and non-deterministic-binary trade-offs that surfaced empirically in S2.
